shots.visual_event: As the city fails, Saira finally stands at Rohan’s bicycle shop door, still sixteen while he is thirty-six.
Rohan compares her to the missing poster in his wallet and touches the matching compass tattoo on his arm.
shots.dialogue_audio: Rohan: “You carried me through the fire.”

shots.visual_event: The exchange plaque manifests between them and demands a memory; Saira turns away to protect him.
shots.dialogue_audio: Saira: “I won’t let it take from you.”

shots.visual_event: Rohan deliberately places his hand on the plaque and offers the memory of learning to ride his first bicycle with her.
shots.dialogue_audio: Rohan: “You already saved my whole life. Take one morning.”

shots.visual_event: The plaque turns cyan instead of red. Saira becomes fully anchored in the present; no unrelated person or place disappears.
Rohan cannot remember the first ride, but knows exactly who Saira is and embraces her.
